english-grammar.q: When I called, Ali ____ dinner.
english-grammar.e: The past continuous shows the background action in progress when another past action occurred.

english-grammar.q: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun “advice” correctly?

english-grammar.e: “women” is the correct plural form of “woman.”

english-grammar.e: “criteria” is the correct plural form of “criterion.”

english-grammar.e: “analyses” is the correct plural form of “analysis.”

english-grammar.q: The person to ____ Ali spoke was the director.
english-grammar.e: After the preposition “to,” formal grammar requires the objective relative pronoun “whom.”

english-grammar.q: The blue folders are ours; the green ones are ____.
english-grammar.e: A possessive pronoun stands alone, so “theirs” is required.

english-grammar.q: The train ____ at 6:30 tomorrow morning.
english-grammar.e: The present simple is used for fixed timetables and schedules.

english-grammar.q: The study examined three ____ in detail.
english-grammar.e: “phenomena” is the correct plural form of “phenomenon.”

english-grammar.q: The rules ____ by every employee.
english-grammar.e: A modal passive is modal + be + past participle.

english-grammar.q: How long ____ you ____ here?
english-grammar.e: A situation extending up to the present commonly takes the present perfect.

english-grammar.q: In British English, choose the sentence that treats “jury” as individual members.
o: The jury are divided in their opinions.
The jury are divided in its opinion.
The jury have divided in its opinions.
The jury is divided in its opinions.
english-grammar.e: A collective noun may take a plural verb in British English when its members act separately.

english-grammar.q: Ali ____ in Karachi for five years, but now lives elsewhere.
english-grammar.e: A finished period that no longer continues takes the past simple.

english-grammar.q: I ____ the door and ____ into the room.
english-grammar.e: Successive completed past actions are normally narrated in the past simple.

english-grammar.q: By next month, Ali ____ here for ten years.
english-grammar.e: The future perfect continuous emphasises duration up to a future point.

english-grammar.q: This is the researcher ____ discovered the error.
english-grammar.e: “Who” is the subject of the relative clause “who discovered the error.”

english-grammar.q: Neither of the answers explains ____ clearly.
english-grammar.e: “Neither” is grammatically singular, so the reflexive pronoun is “itself.”

english-grammar.q: I will call you as soon as the meeting ____.
english-grammar.e: Future time clauses after “as soon as” normally use the present simple, not “will.”

english-grammar.q: We ____ the director at noon tomorrow; the appointment is confirmed.
english-grammar.e: The present continuous can express a definite personal arrangement.

english-grammar.q: Look at those dark clouds; it ____ rain.
english-grammar.e: “Be going to” expresses a prediction based on present evidence.

english-grammar.q: Someone has stolen the files. Choose the passive sentence.
english-grammar.e: The present perfect passive is have/has been + past participle.

english-grammar.q: People believe that the plan is effective. Choose the impersonal passive.
o: It has believed the plan effective.
The plan is believing to be effective.
It believes that the plan is effective.
It is believed that the plan is effective.
english-grammar.e: The impersonal passive uses “It + be + past participle + that-clause.”

english-grammar.q: Water ____ at 100°C at sea level.
english-grammar.e: The present simple states a general scientific fact.

english-grammar.q: I ____ what you mean.
english-grammar.e: Stative verbs such as “understand” are not normally used in the continuous for a present state.

english-grammar.q: This is the first time I ____ this software.
english-grammar.e: “This is the first time…” is normally followed by the present perfect.

environment.q: Which term means “Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem”?
environment.e: Mangrove: Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem. Protects shorelines and stores carbon

environment.q: Which term means “Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels”?
environment.e: Biomagnification: Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels. Classic example involves mercury

environment.q: Which term means “Reduction in stratospheric ozone”?
environment.e: Ozone depletion: Reduction in stratospheric ozone. Strongly linked to chlorofluorocarbons

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances”?
environment.e: Montreal Protocol: Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances. Adopted in 1987

environment.q: Which term means “Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration”?
environment.e: Ozone layer: Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration. Absorbs much harmful ultraviolet radiation

environment.q: Which term means “Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change”?
environment.e: Paris Agreement: Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change. Adopted in 2015

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other”?
environment.e: Commensalism: Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other. One species gains shelter or transport

environment.q: Which term means “Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected”?
environment.e: Exposure: Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected. A component of climate risk

environment.q: Which term means “Framework treaty for international climate cooperation”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
environment.e: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change: Framework treaty for international climate cooperation. Opened for signature in 1992

environment.q: Which term means “Establishment of forest on land not recently forested”?
environment.e: Afforestation: Establishment of forest on land not recently forested. Can increase carbon stocks when appropriately planned

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host”?
environment.e: Parasitism: Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host. Usually does not immediately kill the host

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries”?
environment.e: Kyoto Protocol: Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries. Adopted in 1997

environment.q: Which term means “Conversion or removal of forest cover”?
environment.e: Deforestation: Conversion or removal of forest cover. Reduces habitat and carbon storage

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource”?
environment.e: Competition: Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource. Can occur within or between species

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing”?
environment.e: Convention on Biological Diversity: Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing. Opened for signature in 1992

environment.q: Which term means “Land degradation in drylands”?
environment.e: Desertification: Land degradation in drylands. Driven by climatic variation and human activities

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another”?
environment.e: Predation: Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another. Influences population dynamics

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting both participating species”?
environment.e: Mutualism: Interaction benefiting both participating species. Pollination is a common example

environment.q: Which term means “Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions”?
environment.e: Resilience: Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions. Applies to communities and ecosystems

environment.q: Which term means “Convention regulating international trade in endangered species”?
environment.e: CITES: Convention regulating international trade in endangered species. Uses appendices with different protection levels

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury”?
environment.e: Minamata Convention: Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury. Adopted in 2013

environment.q: Which term means “Population growth slowing near carrying capacity”?
environment.e: Logistic growth: Population growth slowing near carrying capacity. Produces an S-shaped curve

environment.q: Which term means “Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation”?
environment.e: Greenhouse effect: Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation. Natural process intensified by added greenhouse gases

environment.q: Which term means “Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects”?
environment.e: Adaptation: Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects. Can reduce harm or exploit beneficial opportunities

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands”?
environment.e: Ramsar Convention: Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands. Adopted in 1971

environment.q: Which term means “Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems”?
environment.e: Wetland: Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems. Provides flood regulation and habitat

environment.q: Which term means “Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation”?
environment.e: Greenhouse gas: Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation. Examples include carbon dioxide and methane

environment.q: Which term means “Potential occurrence of an event causing harm”?
environment.e: Hazard: Potential occurrence of an event causing harm. Examples include floods and heatwaves

environment.q: Which term means “Accumulation of salts in soil”?
environment.e: Salinization: Accumulation of salts in soil. Often associated with irrigation and poor drainage

environment.q: Which term means “Long-term statistical pattern of weather”?
environment.e: Climate: Long-term statistical pattern of weather. Usually assessed over decades

environment.q: Which term means “Propensity to be adversely affected”?
environment.e: Vulnerability: Propensity to be adversely affected. Depends on exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity

environment.q: Which term means “Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
environment.e: Soil erosion: Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents. Can reduce agricultural productivity

environment.q: Which term means “Short-term atmospheric conditions”?
environment.e: Weather: Short-term atmospheric conditions. Includes temperature, precipitation and wind

environment.q: Which term means “Long-term rise in global average surface temperature”?
environment.e: Global warming: Long-term rise in global average surface temperature. A major component of current climate change

environment.q: Which term means “Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance”?
environment.e: Nitrous oxide: Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance. Major human source is agricultural soil management

environment.q: Which term means “Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks”?
environment.e: Mitigation: Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks. Renewable energy and efficiency are examples

environment.q: Which term means “Long-term change in climate state or variability”?
environment.e: Climate change: Long-term change in climate state or variability. Human influence is the dominant cause of recent warming

environment.q: Which term means “Study of interactions among organisms and their environment”?
environment.e: Ecology: Study of interactions among organisms and their environment. Foundation of ecosystem analysis

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Community.
o: High risk of extinction in the wild
Charismatic species used to mobilize conservation support
Populations of different species living together
Species with a disproportionately large ecological effect
environment.e: Community: Populations of different species living together. Species interact through competition, predation and mutualism

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Population.
o: Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels

System aiming to reduce waste and keep materials in use

Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets
environment.e: Nitrogen cycle: Movement and transformation of nitrogen in ecosystems. Includes fixation and denitrification

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Carbon cycle.

Long-term rise in global average surface temperature
Long-lived greenhouse gas from natural and human sources

Linear transfer of energy through feeding relationships

Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval

Species used to assess environmental conditions

Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance
